result.title: Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation via Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations
result.summary: Specifying segmentation targets with natural language provides flexible semantic conditioning for medical image segmentation. However, existing methods still struggle to reliably ground high-level textual semantics into accurate pixel-level spatial prompts, especially under low-contrast lesions, ambiguous boundaries, and visually similar anatomical contexts. In this paper, we propose RADAR (Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations), a parameter-efficient framework for text-guided medical image segmentation. RADAR explicitly decouples and synergizes the medical semantic anchoring capability of BiomedCLIP with the prompt-driven mask decoding ability of MedSAM2, while enabling low-cost task adaptation via LoRA. Specifically, Guided Residual Depth Aggregation adaptively aggregates cross-layer features under semantic guidance to alleviate delayed textual injection and deep semantic dilution. Structured Dense Representation Alignment leverages a frozen BiomedCLIP to construct crop-level target, boundary, and context anchors, improving the local discriminability of dense features and the reliability of automatic prompts. Multi-modal Prompt Generation further converts cross-modal semantic responses into composite text, point, and mask prompts for MedSAM2 decoding. Experiments on three public medical image segmentation datasets show that RADAR achieves competitive performance with only 0.74M trainable parameters, demonstrating its effectiveness in parameter-efficient adaptation, semantic grounding, and dense representation enhancement. The source code is available at https://github.com/JGuiidev/RADAR.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RADAR 参数高效框架，用 LoRA 将 BiomedCLIP 的语义锚定与 MedSAM2 的提示解码解耦并结合，通过跨层残差聚合、密集表示对齐与多模态提示生成提升文本引导的医学图像分割精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 属医学分割的任务应用型工作，改进点是文本到掩码的空间对齐与提示构造，未涉及 VLM 推理状态生成、视觉旁路、证据获取或停止决策等主线问题，也未提供可迁移的 latent 推理线索，故排除。
